correctness.rationale: For every complex t≠0 the line restrictions have discriminant 8(t−8), finite vertices lie on the conic only at t=16, and the conic misses line intersections at infinity. Bézout and local analytic singularity normal forms therefore give generic 14A1 (τ=14), t=8 6A1+4A3 (τ=18), t=16 2A1+4D4 (τ=18). An independently built Q[t] coefficient matrix for the Jacobian maps in degrees 1–4 was Smith-reduced by four exponent-parity blocks: d=2 exceptional t−16; d=3 exceptional t−8/t−16; d=4 generic kernel dimension four and only these additional specializations for t≠0. This certifies mdr 4/3/2 uniformly, not from finite t-samples. Applying Gałecka Theorem 3.2 yields exactly t=8,16 nearly-free and no free member. The t=0 reducible-conic boundary is explicitly excluded.
residual_risks: Smith form computations are exact over Q[t] and require characteristic zero; not asserted in finite characteristic.

residual_risks: Contribution is this restricted pencil, not arbitrary four-line conic arrangements.
